name: Arm raise to the side
movement: facing the phone, one straight arm raised out to the side to shoulder height and lowered

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, facing you. Stand square to it, both arms in the picture.

words.hint: Facing the phone, one straight arm raised out to the side to shoulder height.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Stand facing it, arms by your sides, whole body in the picture.
words.position: Stand facing the phone, feet hip-width apart, both arms hanging by your sides, palms forward or thumbs up.
words.top: One straight arm raised out to the side to shoulder height — level, not above — the shoulder down, the trunk upright and still.
howto: Stand facing the phone, arms by your sides, palm facing forward, thumb pointing out on the working hand.
Raise the arm out to the side, slowly, to shoulder height, the thumb turning up as it rises. Keep the elbow straight and the trunk upright.
Hold for the count with the shoulder down, away from the ear.
Lower slowly. The rep counts when the arm is back by your side.
words.cannot: Whether the shoulder blade is turning as it should, and an elbow that bends toward the phone: with the thumb up the forearm bends toward the camera, which a front view barely sees. It sees the arm’s angle, the shoulder rising and the trunk leaning.
words.about: Arm raise to the side — facing the phone: the raise, as the angle at the shoulder between the hip and the wrist, 80–110° at the top (90 is level); a rep is under way past 45 and counts when the arm is back under 25; the working shoulder no more than 8° higher than at the start, which is a shrug; the trunk not leaning away from the arm, within 7° of where it started; and the elbow at least 150°. Hold two seconds at the top. A frozen shoulder may stop well short of 90 — set the top where it comfortably reaches and raise it as it frees.
words.lost: Stand facing the camera, both arms in the picture
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: To the point of stretch, not pain. If the shoulder catches on the way up, turn the thumb up and try a little lower.
words.easier: A lower top; a shorter hold; no weight.
words.harder: A light weight; a longer hold; a slow count down.
words.mistakes: Leaning the trunk away to gain height; hiking the shoulder toward the ear; bending the elbow; swinging the arm up.

measurements.label: arm out to the side
measurements.why: The angle at the shoulder between the hip and the wrist, seen from the front: by the side about 15, level 90. Also the progress measurement.

settings.label: Arm angle at the top, at least (90 is level)
Arm angle at the top, at most

measurements.label: shoulder above the other
measurements.why: The line between the shoulders, as its change since the start, so a resting tilt of your own is not called a shrug: the working shoulder rising toward the ear. A little rise is normal past ninety degrees; eight is well beyond it.

settings.label: Working shoulder above the other, at most (degrees)

measurements.label: trunk lean

settings.label: Trunk lean from the start, at most

measurements.why: The working side's hip-to-shoulder line, as its change since the start: leaning the trunk away from the arm tilts it toward the other side (−) and is the commonest way to make a low arm look higher.

measurements.label: elbow straight
measurements.why: The arm straight: under 150 the elbow is bending to shorten the lever.

prompt.text: Raise the arm out to the side

faults.label: Leaning away
faults.text: Trunk upright — don’t lean away from the arm
faults.deep: Lower the arm until you can stay upright

faults.label: Shoulder hiking
faults.text: Shoulder down — don’t hike it toward the ear
faults.deep: The shoulder is up by your ear — let it drop and lower the arm a little

settings.label: Arm angle that counts as under way
